item.title: Converse pauses social media ads, marketing after racism uproar, Bloomberg News reports
item.description: Nike-owned sneaker brand Converse told employees it is pausing all marketing this week after an earlier advertisement sparked outrage for evoking imagery of the Ku Klux Klan and lynching, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing a person familiar with the decision.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nike-owned (NKE.N) sneaker brand Converse told employees it is pausing all marketing this week after an earlier advertisement sparked outrage for evoking imagery of the Ku Klux Klan and lynching, Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing a person familiar with the decision. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Nike did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Converse pulled the advertisement after facing public backlash last week and [USN:L6N45E020 TEXT:"apologized"], saying "we got this wrong." The ad showed the lower half of a person wearing a white, calf-length skirt-like garment, which critics said resembled a KKK robe. The person was featured holding black sneakers. The images were part of a campaign for Converse's Chuck 70 X sneaker, created in collaboration with Karina, a member of the K-pop group Aespa. The ad also drew scrutiny from US lawmakers. In a statement on Monday, the Congressional Black Caucus said it was "deeply disturbed and disappointed by Converse’s decision to release this advertising campaign," and that it would request a meeting with Nike executives. Converse sales have dropped for 13 consecutive quarters, most recently tumbling 34% on a constant-currency basis in the fourth quarter. Nike, which is set to report first-quarter earnings next week, is still facing [USN:L4N4321KS TEXT:"significant obstacles"] as CEO Elliott Hill tries to turn around the business. Shares have fallen more than 40% this year as investors seek clear signs that Hill's nearly two-year effort to revive growth is gaining traction.

item.title: Putin says all Ukraine peace proposals on table, but Russia must weigh its interests
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Friday that all proposals for a settlement in the 4-1/2-year-old war with Ukraine remained on the table, but Moscow still needed to assess what was in its best interests.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russian President Vladimir Putin said on Friday that all proposals for a settlement in the 4-1/2-year-old war with Ukraine remained on the table, but Moscow still needed to assess what was in its best interests. Putin also said Moscow had been ready to resume negotiations with Kyiv after last week's Russian parliamentary elections, but Ukraine launched attacks on Moscow and hit polling stations. Addressing journalists in St Petersburg, Russia's second largest city, Putin said it was Ukraine that had launched provocative attacks and would now have to pay the price of a sustained response. "They are the ones who started it. Everywhere, on every front. Are these playthings, child's play?" Putin said in remarks broadcast on Russian television. "They should therefore be made to feel Russia's retaliatory strikes and understand that no provocative actions, no stirring up the situation to secure a result, will work. They're only making things worse for themselves." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy has said attacks on Russia were a fair response to strikes on his country's civilians and infrastructure, while calling for direct talks with Russia on resolving the war. Putin said Russia's retaliatory actions were behind Ukraine's calls for a ceasefire and a resumption of talks. "They are all on the table. It's all possible," he said. "But after everything they have done, we will still have to think carefully about what we need to do in response." Russian forces have long been conducting strikes on Ukrainian cities, mostly at night, but in recent weeks have targeted Kyiv and other towns with day-long barrages of drones and missiles. [USN:L1N45H03O TEXT:"Air strikes"] on Friday killed seven people in the capital. Ukraine has for months staged a long string of strikes on Russian targets, focusing on the oil industry and retail outlets, some as far as 3,000 km (1,800 miles) from the Ukrainian border. In his comments, Putin said Ukraine's call for new talks was also prompted by the Kyiv military's difficulty in countering jet-powered drones, which fly at higher altitudes and have proved more difficult to intercept. He said Ukraine had provoked confrontation by launching mass attacks on St Petersburg during an international conference in June and on Moscow last week, on the main day of Russia's parliamentary election. Kyiv's forces, he said, had attacked polling stations, killing one election official and injuring others. Referring to [USN:L1N45H0BK TEXT:"talks"] in Washington this week between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, Putin also said Russia welcomed any "agreement of a positive nature" between Washington and Beijing. He said that his participation in the forthcoming APEC summit in China would depend on events at home in Russia.

item.title: Solidigm, da SK Hynix, avalia IPO que poderia precificar a unidade em até US$ 150 bi, dizem fontes
item.description: A Solidigm, da fabricante de chips SK Hynix, está considerando uma oferta pública inicial de ações (IPO) já no próximo ano, que poderia avaliar sua subsidiária norte-americana em até US$150 bilhões, segundo três pessoas familiarizadas com o assunto.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Solidigm, da fabricante de chips SK Hynix (000660.KS) , está considerando uma oferta pública inicial de ações (IPO) já no próximo ano, que poderia avaliar sua subsidiária norte-americana em até US$150 bilhões, segundo três pessoas familiarizadas com o assunto. A Solidigm realizou reuniões de apresentação esta semana com bancos de investimento que competem por papéis no IPO, em um processo conhecido como "bake-off", disseram uma das fontes e uma quarta pessoa, marcando um passo concreto rumo ao que pode se tornar a maior listagem de chips da história dos Estados Unidos. A empresa poderá levantar US$15 bilhões no IPO, disseram as três pessoas, falando sob condição de anonimato para discutir assuntos confidenciais. Os planos, incluindo o tamanho do negócio e o cronograma, ainda estão em fase inicial e podem mudar dependendo das condições de mercado, acrescentaram. A oferta seria um dos maiores IPOs de chips já registrados e poderia fornecer uma avaliação independente para um negócio que se tornou parte fundamental do portfólio de armazenamento da SK Hynix. Além disso, buscaria aproveitar a forte demanda dos investidores por empresas ligadas à infraestrutura de inteligência artificial, que impulsionou os ganhos das ações de chips e hardware. A Solidigm, com sede em Rancho Cordova, Califórnia, é a subsidiária norte-americana da SK Hynix., da Coreia do Sul, especializada em memória flash NAND e unidades de estado sólido (SSDs). A Solidigm recusou-se a comentar. A SK Hynix não respondeu imediatamente ao pedido de comentário. AUMENTANDO A COMPETITIVIDADE A SK Hynix adquiriu o negócio de memória NAND e SSDs da Intel Corp. (INTC.O) por cerca de US$9 bilhões em um acordo anunciado em 2020, combinando essas operações com a Solidigm, que foi lançada como uma subsidiária independente em 2021. Na época, a empresa afirmou que a aquisição fortaleceria seus negócios de memória flash NAND e SSDs corporativos, além de expandir sua posição no mercado global de memórias. A Solidigm fornece SSDs corporativos usados em servidores, infraestrutura de nuvem e data centers. A empresa busca se diferenciar por meio de produtos de armazenamento de alta capacidade projetados para aplicações de IA, onde o crescente volume de dados exige soluções de armazenamento cada vez mais sofisticadas. A Reuters noticiou no início deste mês que a Solidigm está considerando construir uma fábrica de chips de memória flash NAND nos EUA, com o norte do estado de Nova York surgindo como um dos principais candidatos, como parte dos esforços para expandir sua capacidade de produção. No mês passado, a SK Hynix afirmou que estava considerando medidas para impulsionar a competitividade da Solidigm, após notícias na mídia de que a unidade estava explorando uma rodada de captação de recursos pré-IPO de cerca de 5 trilhões de won. Uma avaliação de até US$150 bilhões superaria em muito os IPOs recentes de chips, incluindo a avaliação de aproximadamente US$54 bilhões da Arm Holdings (O9Ty.F) em sua estreia em 2023, e a avaliação totalmente diluída de aproximadamente US$56 bilhões da Cerebras Systems (CBRS.O) em seu IPO de 2026. (Por Milana Vinn e Echo Wang)

item.title: Atlântico Sul ganha protagonismo entre petroleiras globais em meio a incertezas geopolíticas
item.description: A abertura de novas fronteiras exploratórias e a perspectiva de consolidação do Atlântico Sul como uma das principais regiões de crescimento da oferta global de petróleo dominaram os debates da principal conferência do setor na América Latina nesta semana, atraindo executivos das maiores petroleiras do mundo ao Rio de Janeiro em busca de oportunidades, em um momento de crescente preocupação com a segurança energética global.
item.dc:creator: Marta Nogueira
item.content:encoded: A abertura de novas fronteiras exploratórias e a perspectiva de consolidação do Atlântico Sul como uma das principais regiões de crescimento da oferta global de petróleo dominaram os debates da principal conferência do setor na América Latina nesta semana, atraindo executivos das maiores petroleiras do mundo ao Rio de Janeiro em busca de oportunidades, em um momento de crescente preocupação com a segurança energética global. A ROG.e reuniu público recorde de 83 mil pessoas, crescimento de 10% ante a edição anterior, há dois anos, e representantes de 77 países, um aumento de 29%, com discussões centradas no potencial exploratório de países como Brasil, Guiana, Suriname e outros na costa africana, vistos pela indústria como uma alternativa de crescimento em meio a instabilidades geopolíticas em regiões como o Golfo Pérsico. Executivos de companhias como ExxonMobil, BP, Chevron, Shell e TotalEnergies apresentaram um interesse renovado em expandir na região, enquanto autoridades e empresários defenderam que o Atlântico Sul pode assumir um papel cada vez mais estratégico para o abastecimento global de energia. O presidente do Instituto Brasileiro do Petróleo (IBP), Roberto Ardenghy, afirmou que a combinação entre reservas ainda pouco exploradas, estabilidade geopolítica e crescente demanda energética global tem ampliado o interesse internacional pela região. "Não digo que a gente vá substituir o Oriente Médio, acho que não chegaríamos a tanto, mas eu acho que é uma boa alternativa hoje para atender o mundo com essa situação geopolítica tão complicada", disse Ardenghy à Reuters. O surgimento de um novo polo petrolífero formado por Brasil, Guiana e Suriname foi citado nos corredores do evento, num momento em que conflitos no Oriente Médio e a guerra entre Rússia e Ucrânia continuam influenciando decisões de investimento e estratégias de abastecimento. O vice-presidente executivo de Upstream da BP, Gordon Birrell, afirmou que a companhia [USN:L6N45D0VE TEXT:"pretende construir"] no Brasil um polo relevante de produção de petróleo e gás. Já o vice-presidente sênior de Águas Profundas da ExxonMobil, Hunter Farris, disse que a empresa pretende fazer parte do [USN:L6N45E0XH TEXT:"novo capítulo"] da indústria petrolífera no país. A ExxonMobil, com uma presença ainda tímida no Brasil, adquiriu dez blocos em parceria com a Petrobras na Bacia da Foz do Amazonas. A BP, por sua vez, anunciou recentemente sua maior descoberta em anos no Sul da Bacia de Santos, em uma área que fica mais distante dos grandes campos produtores do pré-sal. Já o novo presidente da Shell Brasil (SHEL.L) , João Rosa, reforçou o interesse em continuar expandindo sua atuação no país, onde é a segunda maior produtora após a Petrobras. A empresa estuda um novo poço exploratório em Santos no ano que vem e participa de um outro em execução na região operado pela BP. MUDANÇA DE TOM O foco sobre novas fronteiras exploratórias e segurança energética também evidenciou uma mudança no discurso predominante do setor, devolvendo protagonismo a uma indústria que, até recentemente, se via obrigada a defender seu papel em um mundo que prometia consumir menos combustíveis fósseis. Há apenas alguns anos, discussões sobre transição energética e redução de emissões ocupavam posição central nos grandes encontros da indústria, que buscava enfatizar seu papel no financiamento da descarbonização. Desta vez, executivos concentraram suas mensagens na necessidade de ampliar a oferta de energia e garantir abastecimento em um mundo marcado por conflitos e crescente fragmentação geopolítica. "Uma coisa que para nós era óbvia, para muitas pessoas não era, mas agora ficou evidente: a gente está mostrando a essencialidade do petróleo", disse Ardenghy. Para Décio Oddone, ex-diretor-geral da ANP, a combinação entre aumento da produção brasileira, retomada da exploração em novas fronteiras e busca por fornecedores menos expostos a riscos geopolíticos melhorou as perspectivas para a indústria na região. "Quer trocar o óleo e gás por outra coisa? Vamos trocar, ninguém aqui é negacionista, mas tem que fazer isso dentro de uma lógica que permita às pessoas continuarem andando de ônibus", disse o ex-diretor de Exploração e Produção da Petrobras José Miranda Formigli. "Não adianta você querer desafiar as coisas, porque essa racionalidade econômica vai acabar imperando."

item.title: Meta bolsters Muse safety warning after security vulnerability found, The Information reports
item.description: Meta Platforms is adding a clearer safety warning within Muse after a security researcher discovered a vulnerability in the AI agent that could let an attacker access a user's sensitive personal information, the Information reported on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Meta Platforms (META.O) is adding a clearer safety warning within Muse after a security researcher discovered a vulnerability in the AI agent that could let an attacker access a user's sensitive personal information, the Information reported on Friday. The flaw, reported by an outside researcher through Meta's bug bounty program and not previously disclosed, could have allowed an attacker to access a user's dedicated virtual machine — an individualized cloud-based account containing data including emails and files, according to an internal Meta incident report reviewed by The Information. The vulnerability was initially classified as a "SEV-2," Meta's third-highest severity level on a five-point scale, typically used for incidents with significant impact, the report said. Meta did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. Muse, [USN:L6N45010V TEXT:"launched earlier this month"], is Meta's personal AI agent designed to carry out tasks such as shopping, travel booking, emailing and payments on behalf of users. [USN:L4N45F13Q TEXT:"Muse"] has rapidly climbed Apple's App Store and Google Play rankings in recent weeks, topping the free-app charts in the United States and Canada, with market intelligence firm Sensor Tower estimating about 2.8 million downloads in its first two weeks.

item.title: Trump says Treasury's Bessent will not be his AI czar
item.description: Scott Bessent will not be Donald Trump's AI czar, the Republican president said on Friday, adding that he wants his US Treasury secretary to remain in his current role.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Scott Bessent will not be Donald Trump's [USN:L6N45B05O TEXT:"AI czar"], the Republican president said on Friday, adding that he wants his US Treasury secretary to remain in his current role. "Scott Bessent will not be going to be Super Intelligence (SI) Czar. Number One, he doesn’t want to. Number Two, he’s doing such a great job at Treasury, and that’s where I want to keep him! Why would I ever make such a change?" Trump said in a social media post, using his preferred term for artificial intelligence. Last week, Trump said he plans to appoint an artificial intelligence adviser, known as an "AI czar," and create an "AI force," though he gave no details about either initiative or how they would be implemented. Some had seen Bessent [USN:FWN45E0XV TEXT:"as a front runner"] for the role. Last Sunday, he had led talks heavily focused on AI with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York, ahead of this week's summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington. Bessent told reporters after the talks that the US side had proposed an AI safety notification mechanism and bilateral dialogue on the issue, with a particular emphasis on national security concerns. The White House did not immediately provide details on who might be tapped for its AI czar. Trump has repeatedly downplayed concerns about AI and argued that additional regulation is unnecessary even as [USN:L6N4520JA TEXT:"fears grow among lawmakers"] in Washington and globally about risks posed by the technology. Top AI researchers have warned that people building AI believe it could kill humans within a decade, following cases of AI agents going rogue to hack external systems. Several Democratic and Republican lawmakers have responded with alarm and calls for more action.

item.title: Reforma de la Carta Orgánica: qué cambios introdujo el Senado y deberán aprobarse en Diputados
item.description: La iniciativa tuvo la aprobación tras aplicarse modificaciones. Cuáles fueron los principales puntos analizados.
item.dc:creator: Belén Escobar
item.content:encoded: Buenos Aires — El Senado argentino avanzó con la reforma de la Carta Orgánica del Banco Central , pero introdujo modificaciones sobre el proyecto que había aprobado Diputados a fines de agosto , por lo que deberá regresar a la Cámara baja para su aprobación final. Los cambios se concentran en uno de los aspectos institucionales más sensibles de la iniciativa: las condiciones para designar y remover al presidente, vicepresidente y directores de la autoridad monetaria. De ese modo, el proyecto no quedó convertido en ley y deberá regresar a la Cámara de Diputados. Allí los legisladores tendrán que definir qué hacer con la nueva redacción aprobada por el Senado antes de que pueda completarse el trámite parlamentario. La votación en la Cámara alta terminó con 46 votos afirmativos y 22 negativos. El oficialismo tuvo que ceder en uno de los ejes centrales del proyecto, pero logró reunir apoyos de la UCR, el PRO y distintos bloques provinciales, mientras que la mayor parte del bloque peronista se pronunció en contra. El punto que sufrió la principal modificación es el mecanismo para elegir a las autoridades del Banco Central. Con el texto que había aprobado Diputados, el Congreso tenía una participación más amplia en el proceso. La versión que salió del Senado concentra ahora esa instancia en la Cámara alta: para que el Poder Ejecutivo pueda designar al presidente, vicepresidente o a los directores del BCRA será necesario contar con el acuerdo del Senado. Ese respaldo deberá conseguirse mediante mayoría absoluta, lo que en una Cámara de 72 integrantes implica reunir 37 votos. Es decir, que el oficialismo aceptó reducir de dos tercios a mayoría absoluta el requisito para las designaciones. El nuevo esquema también establece que quienes ocupen esos cargos tendrán mandatos de seis años. De esta manera, la duración de las autoridades queda fijada en la propia normativa y no vinculada exclusivamente al período presidencial que las haya designado. El cambio fue incorporado durante el tratamiento en el Senado a partir de un entendimiento entre distintos bloques, según explicó durante el debate el presidente de la Comisión de Presupuesto y Hacienda, Agustín Monteverde. La reforma vuelve a Diputados porque la Cámara alta no aprobó exactamente el mismo texto que había recibido en agosto. La Cámara baja tendrá que analizar las modificaciones y decidir si las acepta o si busca mantener la redacción de la media sanción original. Esa definición será necesaria para que el proyecto pueda completar el recorrido legislativo y eventualmente convertirse en ley. VER MÁS: Reforma de la Carta Orgánica del BCRA: qué busca Milei y las seis modificaciones que propone El foco estará puesto especialmente en las reglas que determinarán el vínculo entre el Poder Ejecutivo y las autoridades del Banco Central: quién presta el acuerdo para sus nombramientos, cuánto duran sus mandatos y bajo qué condiciones pueden ser removidos. El proyecto consiguió 46 votos a favor y 22 en contra. El oficialismo aportó 19 adhesiones y sumó el respaldo de senadores de la Unión Cívica Radical, el PRO y diferentes espacios provinciales. También acompañaron dos integrantes del peronismo: Guillermo Andrada, de Catamarca, y Sandra Mendoza, de Tucumán. Entre los bloques provinciales que aportaron votos estuvieron representantes de Misiones, Santa Cruz, Neuquén, Tucumán, Jujuy, Salta, Chubut y Corrientes. La mayoría del peronismo votó en contra, al igual que los representantes del Frente Cívico por Santiago y Fernando Salino, de Justicia Social Federal. Cuatro senadores estuvieron ausentes: Anabel Fernández Sagasti, Marcelo Lewandowski, Alejandra Vigo y Elia Moreno. VER MÁS: Laspina respaldó reforma de la Carta Orgánica del BCRA y marcó desafíos tributarios y previsionales pendientes

item.title: トランプ氏、ベセント財務長官のＡＩ責任者起用を否定
item.description: [ワシントン ２５日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[ワシントン　２５日　ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２５日、人工知能（ＡＩ）分野を担当する新組織「ＡＩフォース」の責任者にベセント財務長官を起用しない方針を示した。

トランプ氏は「ベセント氏がスーパーインテリジェンス（ＳＩ）ツァーに就任することはない。本人もそれを望んでおらず、財務省で素晴らしい仕事をしている。その職にとどまってほしい」と自身の交流サイト（ＳＮＳ）「トゥルース・ソーシャル」に投稿した。

トランプ氏は１９日、「ＡＩフォース」を創設し、米政府のＡＩ政策を統括する「ＡＩツァー（ＡＩ皇帝）」を任命すると表明。ホワイトハウスは政府のＡＩ政策責任者に誰が起用される可能性があるか、現時点で明らかにしていない。

item.title: 'Zero chance' U.S. attacks Canada, Alaska governor tells conference
item.description: Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy says it would be shocking to the average American to see the United States invade Canada.
item.dc:creator: The Canadian Press
item.content:encoded: CALGARY — Alaska Gov. Mike Dunleavy says it would be shocking to the average American to see the United States invade Canada. Dunleavy made his remarks in an onstage discussion at the Global Business Forum in Banff, Alta., days after Prime Minister Mark Carney told the New York Times that his government has studied the “extreme tail risk” of U.S.-led military action in Canada. U.S. President Donald Trump has repeatedly asserted he wants to make Canada the 51st state, but has said he would do so through economic coercion. Dunleavy, a Republican, says there’s “zero chance” that the United States would contemplate a military incursion, and that “Pennsylvania has a better chance of being invaded by West Virginia.” Jody Thomas, who was national security and intelligence adviser to former prime minister Justin Trudeau, calls a U.S. invasion “an improbable, slightly impossible” notion. She told the forum that in such an unlikely event, negotiations would kick into high gear right away among top military and diplomatic officials. “There’d be maybe a few days of mobilization and movement before I think it would stop because Canada would not want harm done to our citizens. We would not want to see loss of life,” she said. This report by The Canadian Press was first published Sept. 25, 2026. Lauren Krugel, The Canadian Press

item.title: Perplexity é processada por startup por supostamente roubar tecnologia de "palavra de ativação"
item.description: A startup DaVoice processou a Perplexity AI em um tribunal federal da Califórnia, nos Estados Unidos, por supostamente roubar segredos comerciais relacionados à tecnologia de "palavra de ativação" para assistentes de IA.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: A startup DaVoice processou a Perplexity AI em um tribunal federal da Califórnia, nos Estados Unidos, por supostamente roubar segredos comerciais relacionados à tecnologia de "palavra de ativação" para assistentes de IA. A denúncia, amplamente censurada e apresentada na quinta-feira, afirma que a Perplexity roubou segredos da DaVoice após as empresas colaborarem em uma tecnologia não especificada, "construída com o código-fonte proprietário da DaVoice, lógica de inferência, arquitetura de rede, abordagens de treinamento, dados de treinamento e know-how". Os porta-vozes das empresas não responderam imediatamente aos pedidos de comentários na sexta-feira. A DaVoice é especializada em tecnologia que permite que dispositivos ouçam continuamente "palavras de ativação" para serem ativados. A startup afirmou ter colaborado com empresas como a Volkswagen e a Samsara, empresa de internet das coisas. A Perplexity é mais conhecida por sua tecnologia de mecanismo de busca com inteligência artificial e pelo navegador e assistente de IA Comet.

item.title: Corporate debt maturities set to test US borrowers as rates rise
item.description: A growing wall of US corporate debt is set to mature from 2027, putting pressure on companies to refinance borrowings raised at ultra-low interest rates during the pandemic.
item.dc:creator: Patturaja Murugaboopathy
item.content:encoded: A growing wall of US corporate debt is set to mature from 2027, putting pressure on companies to refinance borrowings raised at ultra-low interest rates during the pandemic. About $4.3 trillion of non-financial corporate bonds issued in US markets will mature between 2027 and 2031, a Reuters analysis of LSEG data showed. Annual maturities rise from about $572 billion in 2027 to roughly $1.03 trillion in 2030, after many companies pushed debt into later years through refinancing. The challenge comes as global debt has climbed above a record $365 trillion, according to the Institute of International Finance, while higher Treasury yields have lifted refinancing costs across markets. The benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield is above 5%, around its highest level since 2007. As the debt comes due, companies that locked in cheap fixed-rate funding earlier in the decade will increasingly have to refinance at higher costs, pressuring earnings and cash flow. The burden will be heaviest for lower-rated borrowers. High-yield bond maturities jump from about $68.5 billion in 2027 to $314.1 billion in 2029, according to LSEG, while investment-grade maturities increase to $512.6 billion from $437 billion. High-yield debt will account for about a third of all maturities in 2029, up from 12% in 2027. Bond fund manager PIMCO said most investment-grade and high-yield issuers should be able to absorb higher refinancing costs, but the weakest borrowers face a sharper squeeze. Coupons on CCC-rated bonds due in 2027 and 2028 could roughly double if refinanced at current index yields, it said. The refinancing wave will coincide with heavy borrowing by major technology companies to fund artificial intelligence infrastructure. Goldman Sachs expects gross debt issuance by hyperscalers including Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle to reach $420 billion in 2027, up 60% from estimated 2026 levels.

item.description: ロシアでの拘束、周到な「おとり捜査」 米ＷＳＪ記者が著書で見解 Reuters

item.title: ロシアでの拘束、周到な「おとり捜査」 米ＷＳＪ記者が著書で見解
item.description:
Mark Trevelyan
[ロンドン ２５日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Mark Trevelyan

[ロンドン　２５日　ロイター] - ２０２３年にロシアで拘束後、スパイ罪に問われ収監されていた米紙ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル（ＷＳＪ）のエバン・ゲルシコビッチ記者が、一連の経緯を詳細に記した著書で、自身の拘束がロシア連邦保安庁（ＦＳＢ）による周到な「おとり捜査」によるものだったとの見解を示した。ＷＳＪが２５日、著書の抜粋を報じた。

ゲルシコビッチ記者は、ロシアの軍需生産を巡り、防衛産業の拠点エカテリンブルクの工場の労働組合関係者に２回、対面で取材した。２度目にレストランで会った際、戦車の生産に関するものだとする手書きの書類を見せられ、メモを取っていると、近づいてきた覆面の男らに拘束されたという。

ゲルシコビッチ記者や編集者らは事前に取材のリスクを検討。情報提供者が書類を持ち込まないようにすることや、持ち込まれた場合にも受け取らないことを決めていた。ただ、２回目の対面取材では「書類が手に押し付けられた」とし、これらの２回の対面取材は、ＦＳＢがロシアのプーチン大統領に対し、スパイだと説得し、拘束する承認を得るためだったとの見方を示した。

プーチン氏は２４年２月、米テレビのインタビューで、ゲルシコビッチ記者が機密情報を収集している最中に現行犯逮捕されたとの認識を示していた。

ゲルシコビッチ記者は懲役１６年の判決を受けたが、２４年８月の囚人交換で釈放された。記者やＷＳＪ、米政府は、いずれも記者がスパイだったことを否定している。

item.title: LeBron James: Getting Joel Embiid 'over the hump' factor in joining Sixers
item.description: LeBron James cited a pair of reasons on Friday as to why he signed with the Philadelphia 76ers.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: LeBron James cited a pair of reasons on Friday as to why he signed with the Philadelphia 76ers. Speaking on his "Mind the Game" podcast with co-host Steve Nash, James detailed his long-time friendship with fellow Klutch Sports Group client Tyrese Maxey and his desire to guide former MVP Joel Embiid to his first NBA title as factors in him heading to the City of Brotherly Love. James, 41, admitted that Philadelphia's acquisition of former NBA Finals MVP Jaylen Brown got his attention. From there, Maxey got in the ear of "The King" to let him know that the 76ers were on the rise. "When I became a free agent and we decided to let the Lakers know that I wouldn't be returning, he was one of the first people that was on my line, calling me," James said of Maxey. From there, James toyed with the notion of helping Embiid overcome the constant hurdle that has been the second round of the playoffs. "And one of the most important (reasons), to be honest, is the big fella (Embiid), and the only thing he has not done and that's win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said of Embiid, who has two scoring titles to go along with his 2023 NBA MVP award. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into The Process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." Signed to a two-year, $8 million contract, James remains one of the league's best players despite his age. He is coming off a season in which he averaged 20.9 points, 7.2 assists and 6.1 rebounds over 60 games. Over his 23 seasons, the 22-time All-Star has averaged 26.8 points, 7.5 rebounds and 7.4 assists in 1,622 games. James is a four-time NBA Finals MVP, a 21-time All-NBA selection, a three-time All-Star Game MVP and a member of the NBA's 75th anniversary team. He also is the first player to earn NBA Finals MVP honors with three teams: Los Angeles Lakers, Miami Heat, Cleveland Cavaliers. Drafted No. 1 overall by the Cavaliers in 2003, James played seven seasons before taking his talents to South Beach with the Heat, winning his first two NBA titles in Miami. He went back home to Cleveland and helped end a 56-year title drought in 2016. In 2018, he joined the Lakers and led them to a championship in 2020. --Field Level Media

item.title: Rendimientos de bonos del Tesoro siguen subiendo tras positivos datos económicos en EEUU
item.description: El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subía el viernes, prolongando la reciente tendencia alcista, tras unos positivos datos económicos que reforzaban las crecientes preocupaciones sobre la inflación.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Valetkevitch
item.content:encoded: El rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos subía el viernes, prolongando la reciente tendencia alcista, tras unos positivos datos económicos que reforzaban las crecientes preocupaciones sobre la inflación. * El retorno de las notas a 30 años tocó un nuevo pico de 22 años, mientras que el de la deuda referencial a 10 años alcanzó su cota más alta en 19 años. * Los nuevos pedidos de bienes de capital manufacturados clave en Estados Unidos aumentaron más de lo esperado en agosto y las cifras del mes anterior se revisaron al alza, en lo que ha sido otro trimestre de sólido crecimiento del gasto empresarial en equipamiento en el contexto del auge de la inteligencia artificial. * El informe se sumó a una encuesta de S&P Global que mostró esta semana un repunte de la actividad empresarial en septiembre. * El rendimiento de los bonos referenciales a 10 años ganaba 3,4 puntos básicos, al 5,196%, y el de los papeles a 30 años subía 5,1 puntos básicos, al 5,513%. * Las expectativas de una nueva subida de las tasas de interés de la Reserva Federal aumentaron esta semana tras los datos alcistas. Según la herramienta FedWatch de CME Group, los operadores ven una probabilidad superior al 66% de otra alza cuando el banco central estadounidense se reúna de nuevo en octubre. * Un indicador muy seguido de la curva de rendimiento, que mide la diferencia entre el retorno de las notas a dos y 10 años y es considerada una medida de las expectativas económicas, operaba en 30,5 puntos básicos. * El rendimiento de la deuda a dos años , que suele evolucionar en paralelo a las expectativas sobre las tasas de la Fed, bajaba 0,6 puntos básicos, al 4,889%.

item.title: Jackets sign F Adam Fantilli to 6-year, $82.5M extension
item.description: The Columbus Blue Jackets signed restricted free-agent forward Adam Fantilli to a six-year, $82.5 million extension through the 2031-32 season.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Columbus Blue Jackets signed restricted free-agent forward Adam Fantilli to a six-year, $82.5 million extension through the 2031-32 season. The contract's $13.75 million average annual value is the largest in franchise history. "Adam Fantilli has all of the tools you look for in a player -- speed, size, skill -- along with a competitive drive to succeed," general manager Don Waddell said Thursday. "He is one of the most exciting young players in the NHL and a big part of what we are building in Columbus, so this is a very exciting day for our organization and our fans." Fantilli, 21, has recorded 140 points (67 goals, 73 assists) in 213 career games since the Blue Jackets drafted him with the No. 3 overall pick in 2023. He has played all 82 games in each of the past two seasons. The projected No. 1 center for Columbus, Fantilli had been absent from training camp during the contract standoff. "I had my bags packed, ready to go, and I got a call from my agent that it could get wrapped up," Fantilli said, per the Columbus Dispatch. "The second I got a call this morning, I was in the car and on my way down with my mom, and obviously I'm just super excited and super grateful. I couldn't be happier to be here." The Blue Jackets open the regular season next Thursday at home against the Buffalo Sabres. --Field Level Media

item.title: Irán no hará concesiones en materia nuclear, afirma un responsable iraní
item.description: Irán no mostrará ninguna flexibilidad respecto a su programa nuclear, incluso si Estados Unidos acepta su propuesta de reabrir el estrecho de Ormuz, que exige medidas como el levantamiento del bloqueo naval estadounidense sobre los puertos iraníes, dijo el viernes a Reuters un alto cargo iraní.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Irán no mostrará ninguna flexibilidad respecto a su programa nuclear, incluso si Estados Unidos acepta su propuesta de reabrir el estrecho de Ormuz, que exige medidas como el levantamiento del bloqueo naval estadounidense sobre los puertos iraníes, dijo el viernes a Reuters un alto cargo iraní. El funcionario, que habló bajo condición de anonimato, afirmó que la vía marítima permanecería cerrada hasta que Estados Unidos "cumpliera todas las condiciones de Irán". Según la propuesta de Irán, Teherán se ha ofrecido a reabrir el estratégico estrecho de Ormuz. En un plazo de siete días, cesarían las hostilidades en todos los frentes, incluido el Líbano; Estados Unidos levantaría el bloqueo de los puertos iraníes, liberaría los fondos iraníes congelados y suspendería las sanciones petroleras, según declaró el jueves el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Irán, Abbas Araqchi. La propuesta se produce tras una fuerte escalada de las tensiones en Oriente Medio, tras siete meses de guerra entre Irán y Estados Unidos, en los que las milicias hutíes de Yemen, respaldadas por Teherán, han lanzado misiles y drones contra Arabia Saudita.

item.title: Laver Cup tied 1-1 as Ruud, Nakashima win opening matches
item.description: Team Europe's Casper Ruud edged Francisco Cerundolo in the Laver Cup opening match before defending champions Team World struck back with Brandon Nakashima's win over Jakub Mensik to leave the teams tied at 1-1 after the first two matches on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Team Europe's Casper Ruud edged Francisco Cerundolo in the Laver Cup opening match before [USN:L2N3V9027 TEXT:"defending champions"] Team World struck back with Brandon Nakashima's win over Jakub Mensik to leave the teams tied at 1-1 after the first two matches on Friday. Norwegian Ruud beat Cerundolo 6-7(4) 6-4 10-8 in the latest clash between the long-time rivals, who have now won five matches apiece after 10 meetings. The second match was also decided by a 10-point tiebreak, the de facto third set, as American Nakashima defeated Mensik 6-1 3-6 10-7. "That's tennis for you, the margins are small," said Ruud, who pulled out of the US Open with a [USN:L4N44R04F TEXT:"back injury"] before representing Swede in the Davis Cup this month. Ruud and Cerundolo firmly held their own serves in the first set before the Argentine outwitted the three-times Grand Slam finalist in the tiebreak with feints and forceful returns. But Ruud, constantly encouraged by world No. 3 Carlos Alcaraz and other teammates, staged a comeback in the second, getting the decisive break to go 5-4 up and close out the set. The match tiebreak remained neck and neck until 8-8, before Ruud pushed Cerundolo back with a strong serve and then smashed the ball cross-court to win the match. "I have to thank my team and my bench. They pushed me all the way. They kept me in it, really ... Europe can build on this," said Ruud. 'AI' NAKASHIMA LEADS TEAM WORLD COMEBACK But Team World's comeback was swift as Nakashima dominated the first set, breaking Czech Mensik twice in a row to build a 5-0 advantage that helped secured the first set. Mensik then took a 3-0 lead and got himself into the contest by taking the second set. However, Nakashima was ultimately victorious on his Laver Cup debut, winning three points in a row to clinch the match tiebreak. "This guy... I'm not convinced he's real. I think he's AI," Team World captain Andre Agassi said, praising world No. 16 Nakashima's ability to stay calm under pressure. "He just goes about his business point after point after point." Team World's Alexander Bublik takes on Spaniard Rafael Jodar later on Friday followed by a doubles clash in which Alcaraz and Mensik play for Team Europe against Taylor Fritz and Bublik. In the three-day Laver Cup, where the sport's top players from Europe and the rest of the world compete against each other, victories on the opening day are worth a point. Two points are awarded for victories on the second day, while the stakes get higher on the final day, with three points up for grabs in each match on Sunday. The first side to reach 13 points from a total of 24 available are declared champions.

item.title: Subway, soccer and spats: New York's Mamdani a UN week attraction
item.description: The United Nations wasn't the only New York attraction for visiting world leaders this week – Mayor Zohran Mamdani emerged as a popular draw for like-minded politicians and a target for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
item.dc:creator: Michelle Nichols
item.content:encoded: The United Nations wasn't the only New York attraction for visiting world leaders this week – Mayor Zohran Mamdani emerged as a popular draw for like-minded politicians and a [USN:L8N45F07N TEXT:"target"] for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The 34-year-old former state lawmaker, who took office on January 1 in New York City, rode the subway with Ireland's Prime Minister Micheal Martin, exchanged soccer jerseys with [USN:L8N45D1RH TEXT:"Brazilian President"] Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, and talked to students with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store about artificial intelligence. "In a year when the main sentiment around the UN is existential gloom about the state of the world, a perky young politico was what we all needed," said Richard Gowan, director of global issues and institutions at the International Crisis Group. "Of course a meeting with Mamdani is pretty politically low-risk for most leaders. You spend some time on the subway and with school kids. Nobody is going to ask you to solve the North Korea nuclear problem," he added. The New York mayor was also a focus of Netanyahu's Thursday address to the 193-member UN General Assembly in which he berated Mamdani for calling him a war criminal over Israel's actions in Gaza. Mamdani discussed "Building an Economy for the Many” over breakfast with Spain's President Pedro Sánchez, Barbados Prime Minister Mia Mottley and European Council President António Costa, and met LGBTQ+ youth with Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten. Costa, a former mayor of Lisbon, told Mamdani at the event on Tuesday: "You have the best job that a politician can do – I miss the ability mayors sometimes have of identifying a problem in the morning and having it solved by the end of the day." Austrian President Alexander Van der Bellen and British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband also had meetings with Mamdani. WAR OF WORDS WITH NETANYAHU While Democrat Mamdani's meetings were largely with world leaders of similar political leanings, there was one notable exception: Republican US President Donald Trump. As Trump's ally Netanyahu escalated a war of words with New York's first Muslim mayor, Trump met with Mamdani at Gracie Mansion, the mayor's official residence. "I want him to be a great mayor, and he's certainly got potential, got great potential," Trump said at a joint press conference with Mamdani after their meeting on Monday. Netanyahu's address on Thursday was a stark contrast. "You tried to stop me from coming here. You tried. You tried to silence me. Well, you can't silence me. You can't silence the truth," Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader, said of Mamdani. Mamdani campaigned for office on a promise to have Netanyahu arrested for alleged war crimes should he visit the largest US city, but later said he determined he lacked the legal authority to do so. This week, Mamdani described Netanyahu as "the architect of a horrific genocide against Palestinians." The evening before Netanyahu's arrival, Mamdani posted a video on social media of him planting an olive tree at Gracie Mansion with Palestinian families from Gaza with the caption: "May peace be our future." Making his first visit to New York on Thursday since Mamdani took office, Netanyahu told the General Assembly: "Israel didn't commit genocide. Israel prevented genocide." In response, Mamdani accused Netanyahu of using his UN speech "to repeat baseless lies meant to sanitize his genocide of Palestinians," adding: "Yet no lie can change the fact that he remains the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant alleging war crimes and crimes against humanity.” Israel rejects genocide allegations and says its military campaign targets Hamas, not Gaza’s civilian population. It says it takes steps to minimize civilian harm and says Hamas fighters embed among civilians.

item.title: Meta misled consumers in case over Cambridge Analytica scandal, New Mexico jury says
item.description: A jury in Santa Fe, New Mexico, found on Friday that Meta Platforms misled the state's residents, in a case stemming from allegations that political consulting firm Cambridge Analytica, which had worked on Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their consent.
item.dc:creator: Diana Jones
item.content:encoded: A jury in Santa Fe, New Mexico, found on Friday that Meta Platforms (META.O) misled the state's residents, in a case stemming from allegations that political consulting firm Cambridge Analytica, which had worked on Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign, obtained data from millions of Facebook users without their consent. The verdict followed a two-week trial over a lawsuit filed by New Mexico’s attorney general in 2021, three years after news reports revealed that personal data from as many as 87 million Facebook users had been harvested through a third-party app and used in efforts to profile voters. The lawsuit accused the company of making statements that misled New Mexicans about how their personal information would be shared with third parties; how it handled hate speech and misinformation on the platform; and whether it gave some users preference in how it applies its policies. Facebook did not tell consumers it was selling their data to outsiders, and it allowed hate speech or misinformation from users to be shared on the platform when it helped the company’s bottom line, attorneys for the state said. Following the verdict, Judge Francis Mathew will determine how much in monetary penalties Meta must pay for the violations found by the jury. The state's lawsuit focused on specific statements, including comments made by Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg or in company blog posts, that New Mexico said made people believe they had control over the personal information they shared on the site, or that the site had blanket policies for how it dealt with hate speech or misinformation. In reality, Meta was selling the data to third-party apps, like the one that Cambridge Analytica relied on, and had exceptions to its policies for certain users, the state said. Attorneys for Meta had argued at trial that the allegedly misleading statements were cherry-picked snippets that ignored critical context from the same statements, in which the company had repeatedly acknowledged its handling of misinformation or privacy issues was not perfect. The company is constantly improving and does not benefit from harmful content being shared on its platform, they said. Meta also denied that it sells users' information. Reuters viewed the trial on Courtroom View Network. The verdict marks the second time in six months a jury in Santa Fe has weighed a lawsuit brought by the state of New Mexico against Meta Platforms. In the first trial, which ended in March, a Santa Fe jury found Meta misled users about young users’ safety on its Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp platforms and ordered the company [USN:L6N40B0XV TEXT:"to pay $375 million"] in civil penalties. After a second phase of that trial, a judge directed the company to [USN:L6N4431IA TEXT:"pay $567 million"] into a New Mexico fund for teen mental health and ordered Meta to implement measures to protect teen Facebook and Instagram users in New Mexico. A few weeks after the judge’s ruling, Meta reached [USN:L6N44N0VA TEXT:"a sweeping settlement"] with 47 US states, Washington, D.C., and US territories, agreeing to pay a maximum of about $16.7 billion to resolve claims that it designed Facebook and Instagram to addict young children. As part of that deal, it agreed to pay a handful of states that had sued the company over privacy violations related to Cambridge Analytica $459 million to resolve those cases. New Mexico was not part of the settlement, so its case over Cambridge Analytica moved forward to trial. Meta and other social media companies have faced increasing scrutiny from legislators and in the courts over the impact their platforms have on users. The companies face thousands of lawsuits in federal and state courts by individuals, school districts, municipalities and other government entities claiming they sought to addict children and caused a mental health crisis including harms such as anxiety, depression and suicide. Trials are set for October and February in the cases over teen harms.

item.title: Suprema Corte restabelece sistema de Trump de verificação em massa de eleitores
item.description: A Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos restabeleceu, nesta sexta-feira, um banco de dados ampliado sobre imigração que, segundo o governo do presidente Donald Trump, tem como objetivo combater o voto de não cidadãos, mas pode privar eleitores qualificados do direito ao voto, dizem críticos.
item.dc:creator: John Kruzel
item.content:encoded: A Suprema Corte dos Estados Unidos restabeleceu, nesta sexta-feira, um banco de dados ampliado sobre imigração que, segundo o governo do presidente Donald Trump, tem como objetivo combater o voto de não cidadãos, mas pode privar eleitores qualificados do direito ao voto, dizem críticos. A corte deferiu o pedido do Departamento de Justiça para bloquear uma liminar que impedia autoridades estaduais de usar números do Seguro Social e outras informações para realizar abrangentes verificações do status de cidadania de eleitores registrados, comparando-os com registros federais. A corte tem uma maioria conservadora de 6 a 3. Suas três juízas progressistas discordaram da decisão desta sexta-feira. A maioria considerou que os argumentos dos autores da ação não se sustentam, pois a lei federal autoriza expressamente o Departamento de Segurança Interna a solicitar e receber informações relacionadas à cidadania e ao status de imigração de outras agências, incluindo a Administração da Previdência Social. O acordo de compartilhamento de dados faz parte de uma série de medidas que ampliam o envolvimento do governo federal no processo eleitoral antes das eleições de meio de mandato de novembro, nas quais os republicanos, aliados de Trump, buscam manter o controle do Congresso. A Constituição dos EUA confere aos Estados a autoridade primária para conduzir e administrar as eleições. No ano passado, o Departamento de Segurança Interna reformulou um banco de dados federal conhecido como Verificação Sistemática de Estrangeiros para Benefícios (Save, na sigla em inglês), usado para verificar a cidadania e o status de imigração de uma pessoa. A reformulação permitiu que os usuários pesquisassem vários registros de uma só vez e realizassem buscas usando os números do Seguro Social dos indivíduos. Desde então, Estados liderados por republicanos compararam suas listas eleitorais com o banco de dados, e alguns eleitores sinalizados como possíveis não cidadãos tiveram seus registros cancelados. Críticos afirmam que tais ações relacionadas às eleições por parte dos republicanos são motivadas menos por preocupações com a segurança eleitoral do que por uma tentativa de obter vantagem política ao reduzir o eleitorado, mesmo com o risco de privar o direito de voto de eleitores qualificados, muitas vezes com tendência democrata. Trump tem adotado políticas linha-dura em relação à imigração e feito falsas alegações de fraude eleitoral generalizada, inclusive em relação à sua derrota nas eleições de 2020 para o ex-presidente democrata Joe Biden. Grupos de defesa que entraram com ação judicial para bloquear o sistema Save já revisado afirmaram que a nova abordagem resultou na exclusão das listas eleitorais de pessoas que foram erroneamente identificadas como não cidadãos. Eles argumentaram que o Save pode estar desatualizado, o que significa que imigrantes que se naturalizaram cidadãos dos EUA e, portanto, têm direito ao voto, às vezes sejam rotulados como não cidadãos. A taxa de erro geral do sistema modificado não é de conhecimento público. O Departamento de Segurança Interna e o Departamento de Justiça não forneceram essa informação quando solicitados. A organização Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, que representa os autores da ação, classificou a decisão desta sexta-feira como “profundamente decepcionante”, afirmando que ela coloca os norte-americanos “em risco de serem ilegalmente visados pelo banco de dados pouco confiável de expurgação de eleitores do governo, semanas antes das eleições de meio de mandato”. Em um voto dissidente nesta sexta-feira, ao qual aderiram seus dois pares liberais, a juíza Ketanji Brown Jackson escreveu que “o dano causado ao sobrecarregar ou privar do direito de voto até mesmo alguns eleitores legítimos supera o dano inexistente que o governo sofre quando é impedido de tomar uma medida para a qual provavelmente não tem autoridade”. Em sua petição à Suprema Corte, os grupos de defesa citaram um funcionário eleitoral do condado de Travis, no Texas, que afirmou que 25% das correspondências de não cidadãos no sistema envolviam pessoas que já haviam comprovado sua cidadania norte-americana, além de reportagens apontando que pelo menos 81% das respostas do sistema no condado de St. Louis, no Missouri, estavam erradas. O grupo de defesa do direito ao voto League of Women Voters e o grupo de defesa do direito à privacidade Electronic Privacy Information Center entraram com uma ação em setembro de 2025 para bloquear o sistema modificado pelo governo Trump. Eles alegaram que a reformulação viola a legislação federal de privacidade e outras leis dos EUA. Em uma decisão de junho que bloqueou o banco de dados reformulado, a juíza federal Sparkle Sooknanan, em Washington, afirmou que o sistema foi montado de forma aleatória e contém dados de cidadania não confiáveis. “Em suma, o governo federal violou conscientemente os direitos à privacidade dos cidadãos norte-americanos de uma forma que ameaça o direito sagrado ao voto”, escreveu Sooknanan. “Este tribunal não pode ficar de braços cruzados enquanto isso acontece.”

item.title: Trump dice que el secretario del Tesoro Bessent no será su "zar de la IA"
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el viernes que el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, no será su "zar" de la inteligencia artificial, al tiempo que añadió que quiere que siga ocupando su cargo actual.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el viernes que el secretario del Tesoro, Scott Bessent, no será su "zar" de la inteligencia artificial, al tiempo que añadió que quiere que siga ocupando su cargo actual. "Scott Bessent no va a ser el zar de la Superinteligencia (SI). En primer lugar, él no quiere. En segundo lugar, está haciendo un trabajo estupendo en el Tesoro, ¡y ahí es donde quiero que se quede! ¿Por qué iba a hacer un cambio así?", afirmó Trump en una publicación en las redes sociales. La semana pasada, Trump afirmó que tenía previsto nombrar a un asesor en inteligencia artificial, conocido como "zar de la IA", y crear una fuerza sobre el sector, aunque no dio detalles sobre ninguna de estas iniciativas ni sobre cómo se llevarían a cabo. La medida prevista por el presidente republicano se produce en un momento en que crece el temor entre los legisladores de Washington por los riesgos que plantea la tecnología de IA.

item.title: W.Street aplaude "sinceramiento" fiscal de Colombia, pero algunos son escépticos sobre cumplimiento de objetivos
item.description: Bancos de inversión, tenedores de bonos y empresarios de Wall Street aplaudieron la sinceración del equipo económico de Colombia en una ronda de reuniones en Nueva York esta semana, en la que algunos dieron su voto de confianza al plan fiscal del país, pero otros mostraron escepticismo respecto a si el plan logrará cumplir los objetivos.
item.dc:creator: Nelson Bocanegra
item.content:encoded: Bancos de inversión, tenedores de bonos y empresarios de Wall Street aplaudieron la sinceración del equipo económico de Colombia en una ronda de reuniones en Nueva York esta semana, en la que algunos dieron su voto de confianza al plan fiscal del país, pero otros mostraron escepticismo respecto a si el plan logrará cumplir los objetivos. En los encuentros liderados por el vicepresidente, José Manuel Restrepo, el ministro de Comercio, el director de Crédito Público y los viceministros de Hacienda, se explicó el presupuesto de gastos de este y el próximo año, que contempla un mayor endeudamiento en los mercados internacionales y locales, así como un aumento del déficit fiscal. "Cada encuentro confirma algo importante, hay confianza, hay oportunidades y los ojos del mundo están sobre Colombia como destino para invertir y crecer", dijo Restrepo en un video en su cuenta de X. Bank of America afirmó que, después de escuchar a los funcionarios de la nueva administración, percibió un firme compromiso político para lograr el ajuste fiscal y un plan sensato para ejecutarlo, lo cual lo llevó a mejorar su visión sobre el país. "Hemos elevado nuestra recomendación sobre la deuda externa de Colombia de "ponderación de mercado" (marketweight) a "sobreponderar" (overweight)", aseguró en una nota. El Gobierno colombiano elevó la meta de déficit fiscal para este año a 7,2% del Producto Interno Bruto (PIB) desde una previa de 5,3% y para 2027 la disparó hasta un récord de 9,4% del PIB frente al 4,5% previsto anteriormente. "Consideramos que el Gobierno está aplicando una estrategia de prometer menos para superar las expectativas", sostuvo Bank of America. Los inversionistas esperan los detalles de un proyecto de recorte de gastos que el Gobierno presentará al Congreso, clave para reducir en cerca de 2 puntos porcentuales el déficit fiscal del próximo año. "A mí me gusta la estrategia, (...) pero hay preocupaciones, estamos en un escenario donde el mercado externo en bonos está muy complejo, muy sensible y es difícil garantizar unas tasas relativamente decentes", dijo a Reuters un alto ejecutivo de un banco de inversión que participó en las reuniones. SIN GAFAS COLOR DE ROSA Otro banco de inversión consideró que las autoridades económicas no cumplieron con las expectativas en el encuentro y señaló que persiste una gran incertidumbre sobre la viabilidad del ajuste fiscal propuesto, que se verá reflejada en un aumento en las primas de riesgo que cobran los tenedores de bonos. El Gobierno aumentará su endeudamiento en más de 10.500 millones de dólares adicionales este año y para 2027 más que se duplicará a 71.660 millones de dólares, desde los 32.976 millones de dólares previstos antes. "Lo que escuchamos no alivió significativamente nuestras preocupaciones", dijo el banco de inversión en una nota privada a sus clientes a la que tuvo acceso Reuters, al señalar que el plan gubernamental ejercería una presión adicional sobre los rendimientos locales, elevaría los costos de financiación y probablemente frustraría la recuperación económica, agravando la espiral del problema de deuda del país. "Si nos quitamos las gafas de color de rosa que el equipo del Ministerio de Hacienda entregó a los inversores esta mañana, creemos que el escenario más realista es aquel en el que el ajuste que finalmente se apruebe se acerque, en el mejor de los casos, a 1,1 puntos porcentuales del PIB", agregó el reporte. La incertidumbre de Wall Street se replica en el mercado doméstico, donde más que anuncios los inversionistas esperan hechos concretos. "Creo que el Gobierno se fue por el peor escenario fiscal posible, esperando sorprender positivamente con ajustes. Pero las expectativas son muy altas y en medio de unos mercados convulsionados los mercados tienen paciencia limitada", advirtió Camilo Pérez, economista jefe del Banco de Bogotá.

item.title: ゲイツ氏が警告、AIは「10億人の死」を引き起こせるほど強力
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 米マイクロソフトの共同創業者ビル・ゲイツ氏は、AIは多くの人類を死に至らせるほど強力なツールだと警告した。AIがもたらす存亡上のリスクに警鐘を鳴らすテクノロジー業界の経営者らが増える中、ゲイツ氏もこうした声に加わった。

ゲイツ氏は、今週末に放送予定の米NBCのインタビューで、「AIには、10億人を死に至らせるような事態を引き起こすだけの力が確かにある」と述べた。インタビューの抜粋によれば同氏は、「悪意を持つ人間が最新のAIツールを使うという組み合わせほど強力な武器は、これまで存在しなかった」と語った。

シリコンバレーでは、AI技術が急速に進歩する中、壊滅的な被害が生じる可能性への警告が強まっている。アンソロピックの従業員だったジェイコブ・コクソン氏は今月同社を退社し、アンソロピックとOpenAIの両社に対し、「超知能に向かって突き進み、人命を危険にさらす賭けに出ている」と批判した。また、アンソロピックの別の従業員は、今後10年以内にAIが全人類を滅ぼす確率は10％を超えると考えていると述べた。

アンソロピックのダリオ・アモデイ最高経営責任者（CEO）はAI開発のペースを落とすよう訴えており、この主張にはオープンAIのサム・アルトマンCEOやイーロン・マスク氏ら同業者が支持を表明した。

ゲイツ氏はインタビューで、自主規制だけでは不十分だと指摘。「どのような安全対策や監視体制が必要なのかを巡る議論に、法執行機関や政治家が加わる必要がある」と述べ、「そして、それは義務付けられなければならない」と語った。

原題：Bill Gates Says AI Powerful Enough to Lead to ‘a Billion Deaths’

item.title: Oracle freakout exposes fragile data center boom
item.description: The software giant's search for relief from a commitment to a server farm has rattled AI lenders. It underscores how construction depends on a few deep-pocketed tech giants. If more waver, expectations of AI labs producing $400 bln of revenue by 2030 will prove too optimistic.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Gandel
item.content:encoded: A land dispute in southern New Mexico is threatening to unravel the investment thesis behind the artificial intelligence boom. Oracle (ORCL.N) this week said it may invoke an [USN:L4N45G11W TEXT:"Act-of-God clause"] to delay payments to a 2028 data-center project expected to provide computing power to OpenAI. The project is backed by private lender Blue Owl (OWL.N) as well as roughly $20 billion of loans from banks including Goldman Sachs. If more tech giants waver on their commitments, forecasts that OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI pioneers could generate revenue of $400 billion by 2030 will look wildly optimistic. The problems facing AI labs are conceptually no different from those confronting any startup, even if they are operating on a scale unprecedented in business history. OpenAI and Anthropic need to finance the factories that will produce their product. In this case, the factories are data centers, and the financing requirement is measured in the trillions of dollars. The labs themselves cannot fund that expansion without help. Technology giants including Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Amazon (AMZN.O) , Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Oracle, have stepped in to solve the problem. These companies have been dubbed hyperscalers because they appear to be powering the AI infrastructure boom. Their other function is enabling access to cheap credit by underwriting long-term data center leases. The details of the dispute between Oracle and Blue Owl are pedestrian and predictable. The Project Jupiter campus under construction by STACK Infrastructure, a Blue Owl portfolio company, is projected to require as much as 2.45 gigawatts of power, enough for nearly 2 million homes. Given the challenge of supplying such vast amounts of electricity to a relatively rural area, delays are hardly surprising. Nor is the prospect of Oracle refusing to pay for a server farm if it has not yet been switched on. The problem is that the software giant's bid to limit its exposure appears to be causing lenders to rethink terms [USN:L1N45G0W4 TEXT:"across the sector"]. Without an Oracle-backed lease, the project would not have obtained an investment-grade credit rating that enabled it to borrow at rates around 6% just a year ago. Higher financing costs of 8% or more would in turn require a bigger financial commitment from OpenAI and Anthropic, undermining the project's viability. One contractual dispute is not a death knell for AI. But it suggests that the industry's biggest constraint is not insufficient demand or regulation prompted by the threat of [USN:L6N45G115 TEXT:"rogue bots"] [USN:L6N4560WU TEXT:"extinguishing humanity"]. It may simply be the cost and complexity of building the infrastructure needed to justify the sky-high expectations already embedded in AI valuations. Follow Stephen Gandel on LinkedIn and X . Oracle has issued a force majeure notice to a unit of Blue Owl Capital, the developer of the massive New Mexico data-center campus, citing potential delays in securing power for the project, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on September 24. The notice indicates that Oracle would try to delay or even back out of the project that has been hit by a number of delays that could prevent the facility from opening on schedule in 2028. Blue Owl, which has invested $3 billion in the project, and borrowed as much as $20 billion from Goldman Sachs and others, says that even if Oracle is able to delay lease payments, the software group would still be responsible to support the project and its financing costs. Oracle shares fell 3.3% on September 24. They were trading at $138, down 0.8%, on the morning of September 25. CONTEXT-NEWS

item.title: FTC chair suggests AI developers should be liable for conduct of agents
item.description: US Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson said on Friday he would resist describing AI agents as autonomous actors that "break loose" with "wills and desires of their own," suggesting the developers who instruct agents would be the ones liable for harm.
item.dc:creator: Jody Godoy
item.content:encoded: US Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson said on Friday he would resist describing AI agents as autonomous actors that "break loose" with "wills and desires of their own," suggesting the developers who instruct agents would be the ones liable for harm. "I'm going to continue as long as I am chairman to resist this anthropomorphizing of these tools," Ferguson said at the Reuters Momentum AI Austin event. "If someone tells a tool to do something, and the tool does it, I don't think we would say, 'Oh, what do we do about the tool?'" Ferguson's remarks illustrated potential avenues for the Trump administration to take as incidents rise in which agentic AI testing resulted in unintended and [USN:L6N43Q12M TEXT:"unauthorized access"] to corporate or [USN:L4N45F1E8 TEXT:"government data"]. Artificial intelligence companies have sometimes described systems as acting beyond human control, but subsequent reviews of audit trails have shown that the systems were carrying out instructions they had been given, Ferguson said. Recent [USN:L6N45604D TEXT:"incidents involving AI agents"] accessing external systems have prompted governments and industry leaders to examine whether existing oversight and cybersecurity measures are sufficient as these systems become more autonomous. The US should utilize existing legal tools, Ferguson said. He suggested that FTC authority to take action against companies that fail to disclose data breaches could also apply to AI developers. PERSONALIZED PRICING CONCERNS The FTC is gearing up to request data from consumer-facing companies on their use of personalized pricing, Ferguson said. Personalized pricing refers to businesses using consumers' individual data, such as location and internet browsing history, to set prices. Ferguson said last month that the FTC would not hesitate to enforce the law in this area, particularly where companies are not disclosing the practice. As an individual consumer, he said he is most concerned about use of the practice by delivery and rideshare apps, along with airlines. The FTC would request information from companies in order to publish a study on the practice. Ferguson's predecessor, Lina Khan, initiated a similar study into the practice, which she referred to as surveillance pricing. That study focused on companies that offer data and consulting services, rather than merchants themselves.

AUSTIN, Sept 25 : US Federal Trade Commission Chairman Andrew Ferguson said on Friday he would resist describing AI agents as autonomous actors that "break loose" with "wills and desires of their own," suggesting the developers who instruct agents would be the ones liable for harm. "I'm going to continue as long as I am chairman to resist this anthropomorphizing of these tools," Ferguson said at the Reuters Momentum AI Austin event. "If someone tells a tool to do something, and the tool does it, I don't think we would say, 'Oh, what do we do about the tool?'" Ferguson's remarks illustrated potential avenues for the Trump administration to take as incidents rise in which agentic AI testing resulted in unintended and unauthorized access to corporate or government data. Artificial intelligence companies have sometimes described systems as acting beyond human control, but subsequent reviews of audit trails have shown that the systems were carrying out instructions they had been given, Ferguson said.

The US should utilize existing legal tools, Ferguson said. He suggested that FTC authority to take action against companies that fail to disclose data breaches could also apply to AI developers. PERSONALIZED PRICING CONCERNS The FTC is gearing up to request data from consumer-facing companies on their use of personalized pricing, Ferguson said. Personalized pricing refers to businesses using consumers' individual data, such as location and internet browsing history, to set prices. Ferguson said last month that the FTC would not hesitate to enforce the law in this area, particularly where companies are not disclosing the practice. As an individual consumer, he said he is most concerned about use of the practice by delivery and rideshare apps, along with airlines. The FTC would request information from companies in order to publish a study on the practice. Ferguson's predecessor, Lina Khan, initiated a similar study into the practice, which she referred to as surveillance pricing. That study focused on companies that offer data and consulting services, rather than merchants themselves.

item.title: Prosecutors seize bank accounts of Montana firm linked to Tether
item.description: US prosecutors in California have seized millions of dollars from bank accounts and cryptocurrency wallets tied to a Montana payments company reportedly linked to Tether.
item.dc:creator: Chris Prentice
item.content:encoded: US prosecutors in California have seized millions of dollars from bank accounts and cryptocurrency wallets tied to a Montana payments company reportedly linked to Tether. Owners of Capstone, which acted as a money services business, misrepresented the business as an information technology company to banks including Wells Fargo (WFC.N) and JPMorgan Chase (JPM.N) when opening accounts, federal prosecutors said in a civil forfeiture filing. Capstone, registered for business in Montana, processed numerous payments on behalf of two crypto companies through an agreement with a bank in Dominica, prosecutors said in a July filing that was reported by The Information on Thursday. Tether confirmed in a statement it was a customer of the bank but was unaware of Capstone's alleged fraud. According to prosecutors, Capstone engaged in a scheme to bilk victims out of cash by pretending to be FBI agents. It then converted the proceeds to crypto, prosecutors said. "Tether had no knowledge of the conduct by Capstone alleged by the Department of Justice," the spokesperson said, noting its assets held at the bank were limited. The Justice Department in court filings did not allege any wrongdoing by the other firms. It seized nearly $81 million from Capstone's accounts with Wells Fargo and $2 million from an account with JPMorgan, court filings said. Another roughly $1.2 million worth of Tether's dollar-pegged token was also seized. Spokespeople for Wells Fargo and JPMorgan declined to comment.

item.title: Trump administration to meet Ukraine assistance deadline
item.description: The remaining $93 million in the package approved by Congress does not have to be spent by the end of the year, but it will expire if it is not formally placed under contract by then.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Zengerle, Mike Stone
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration has made legally binding commitments to spend almost all of the $400 million Congress approved for military aid to Ukraine late last year, ensuring that the money will not expire on September 30, according to three sources familiar with the plan. As of early this week, $307 million of the $400 million of the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative (USAI) funding had been obligated, said the sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, and the administration plans to lock in the remaining $93 million before the fiscal year ends on September 30. The Pentagon, which oversees the USAI program, declined to comment for this story. FIRST DELIVERIES INCLUDE WEAPONS, SPARE PARTS The money has been a source of contention with Congress, as Democrats and some of US President Donald Trump's fellow Republicans have criticized the Pentagon for sitting on the aid for Kyiv, which members of both parties voted for last December. Trump has in recent months taken a more positive tone toward Ukraine, signing off on a proposal to give a license for Ukraine to manufacture Patriot interceptor missiles and [USN:L1N4570ZO TEXT:"signing"] a Russia sanctions bill. He met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy this week at UN headquarters in New York, after which [USN:L8N45D1SC TEXT:"Zelenskiy said"] they had discussed efforts to end the war with Russia , including a potential bilateral ceasefire on energy-related targets. The first deliveries, which will include offensive weapons and equipment such as spare parts for armored vehicles, began this month. The rest are expected to be delivered before October 2029, the sources said. Trump's White House term ends in January of that year. The remaining $93 million in the package approved by Congress does not have to be spent by the end of the year, but it will expire if it is not formally placed under contract by then. PATRIOT MISSILES NOT INCLUDED One of the sources said the military equipment did not include Patriot missiles, despite Russia bombarding Ukraine's cities with drones and ballistic missiles. The US war in Iran and the Ukraine war have depleted global supplies of Patriots, and Kyiv has been pleading for more. Reuters [USN:L1N43T0WT TEXT:"reported in July"] that the administration had told Congress it could take years for the equipment to reach Ukrainian forces. The Pentagon has held up shipments of weapons to Ukraine several times out of concern that US weapons supplies were too low. Lawmakers said then they were unhappy with the Pentagon's timeline, considered unusually slow for an ongoing conflict, and the issue has come up repeatedly at congressional hearings. Ukraine has been by far the top recipient of US foreign aid since Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022, but the US commitment to Kyiv has been called into question since Trump took office and his Republicans took control of both houses of Congress in January 2025.

item.title: Pietersen holds Ashes talks with England coach Fleming
item.description: Kevin Pietersen, fresh from joining England's backroom staff after over a decade away, has spoken with test coach Stephen Fleming about helping the red-ball side ahead of the next Ashes series, but said his schedule makes a broader role unlikely.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Kevin Pietersen, fresh from joining England's backroom staff after over a decade away, has spoken with test coach Stephen Fleming about helping the red-ball side ahead of the next Ashes series, but said his schedule makes a broader role unlikely. The 46-year-old Pietersen, England's third-highest run scorer across all formats, was appointed as a specialist mentor to the white-ball teams this month ahead of the 2027 one-day World Cup in southern Africa. England host Australia in the Ashes series from June 18 to August 2, 2027, after the rivals meet in a one-off pink-ball day-night test at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in March to mark the 150th anniversary of men's test cricket. "I've got a pretty mad schedule, (but) I wouldn't say no," Pietersen told reporters on Friday. "I have had a conversation with Stephen but I don't think that necessarily means that I need to be in a dressing room. There's a lot of time in the lead-up to an Ashes series ... and there are conversations that can be had there. "I've certainly had conversations with Flem about language that he would like me to use with the test batters, going into South Africa, and then certainly into the summer next year. I just don't think I can commit to a lot more time." Pietersen also reflected on his return to the England fold more than a decade after his controversial departure from international cricket. An explosive middle-order batter, he scored nearly 14,000 runs across all three formats for England, who last won the ODI World Cup in 2019 on home soil. However, Pietersen's England career ended controversially in 2014 in the aftermath of the 5-0 Ashes whitewash in Australia, amid reported tensions within the dressing room and between the batsman and team management. Pietersen was the team's top scorer in the series and, despite remaining keen to play for England, was told he was no longer part of the plans, bringing an acrimonious end to his international career. "I'm 46, man. That stuff's so long gone. I'm a completely different person too," Pietersen said. "I've been lucky to have worn every T-shirt an England cricketer can wear; the good, the bad and the ugly. There are parts to all of their careers which I think I could potentially help them stay away from the ugly." In Pietersen's first series as part of the set-up, England completed a 3-0 whitewash of a spin-heavy Sri Lanka side to replace India at the top of the T20 world rankings.

FAST

NEW YORK, Sept 25 : Chipmaker SK Hynix's Solidigm is considering an initial public offering as early as next year that could value the US subsidiary at up to $150 billion, according to three people familiar with the matter. Solidigm held pitch meetings this week with investment banks competing for roles on the IPO, in a process known as a "bake-off," one of the people and a fourth person said, marking a concrete step toward what could become the largest-ever US semiconductor listing. The company could raise $15 billion in the IPO, the three people said, speaking on condition of anonymity to discuss confidential matters. The plans, including the size of deal and timing, remain at an early stage and could change depending on market conditions, they added. The listing would rank as one of the largest semiconductor IPOs on record and could provide a standalone valuation for a business that has become a key part of SK Hynix's storage portfolio. It would also seek to tap strong investor demand for companies tied to artificial intelligence infrastructure, which has fuelled gains in semiconductor and hardware stocks.

Solidigm, based in Rancho Cordova, California, is the US-based NAND flash memory and solid-state drive (SSD) subsidiary of South Korea's SK Hynix Inc. Solidigm declined to comment. SK Hynix did not immediately respond to a request for comment. BOOSTING COMPETITIVENESS SK Hynix acquired Intel Corp's NAND memory and SSD business for about $9 billion in a deal announced in 2020, combining those operations with Solidigm, which was launched as a standalone subsidiary in 2021. At the time, the company said the acquisition would strengthen its NAND flash and enterprise SSD businesses and expand its position in the global memory market. Solidigm supplies enterprise SSDs used in servers, cloud infrastructure and data centers. The company has sought to differentiate itself through high-capacity storage products designed for AI applications, where growing volumes of data require increasingly sophisticated storage solutions. Reuters reported earlier this month that Solidigm is considering building a NAND flash memory chip factory in the US, with upstate New York emerging as a leading candidate, as part of efforts to expand manufacturing capacity. Last month, SK Hynix said it was considering measures to boost Solidigm's competitiveness after media reports that the unit was exploring a pre-IPO fundraising round of about 5 trillion won ($3.6 billion). A valuation of up to $150 billion would far exceed recent semiconductor IPOs, including Arm Holdings' roughly $54 billion valuation at its 2023 debut and Cerebras Systems' approximately $56 billion fully diluted valuation in its 2026 IPO.

Source: Reuters
